root.meaning: weft, the cross-threads of a fabric
root.note: Latin trama ‘weft’ is secure. Its own earlier origin is unclear.

stages.meaning: weft; plot of a story; scheme

history: A story is a piece of weaving. In weaving, the warp threads run lengthwise, and the weft threads pass across them. Latin called the weft trama, and Italian kept it: la trama di un tessuto is the weft of a fabric. People then began to speak of a story the same way, as threads woven together to make a pattern, and la trama of a film or a novel is its plot. The verb tramare joins the picture: it means ‘to weave’ and also ‘to plot, to scheme’, as in tramare un complotto. When a reader asks ‘qual è la trama?’, they want the outline of what happens. Spanish and French keep the same two meanings, so the picture is shared across the Romance languages.
historyEinfach: Trama is a Latin word for the cross-threads in a woven cloth. Italian uses it for cloth, and also for the plot of a book or film, because a story has threads woven together. The verb tramare means ‘to weave’ and ‘to plot against someone’.
